The branch-specific extras (Belgian waffle, Cremia matcha, fruit soda, panini, spice curry) come from that same street board. The bakery items and their prices come from a user-submitted listing on Yahoo! Map, not from the shop, and look like older/tax-exclusive figures — treat them as indicative only. toba_hinoyama_lab.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. Unlike MUSEA's town branches, Hinoyama Lab has its OWN printed menu board, branded 'HINOYAMA LAB by MUSEA', with its own (lower) prices — these are transcribed from clear photographs of that board and independently corroborated item-for-item by a Japanese blog write-up, so they have not been blended with the other MUSEA branches. Yen figures are the tax-included ones printed on the board. The 'Today's Menu' half of the board rotates seasonally — kakigori is a summer item. Opening is irregular (Tabelog lists Thu-Sun 12:00-17:00); it stands on the grounds of the ryokan Senpokaku on the slope of Hinoyama, about 13 min / 1 km walk from Toba Station, in a building designed by architect Teppei Fujiwara. Guests can use Senpokaku's car park. It is a confectionery-manufacturing lab with a coffee stand attached, so the puddings are the reason to come.

toba_ephemere.price_note: Prices approximate — may change. These six are the full grand menu, transcribed from a Mie food blog that photographed the board; the college's own announcement and a Chunichi Shimbun news piece independently confirm 'six varieties, ¥500-700 tax included', which matches exactly — hence high confidence despite no shop-published price list being reachable (the shop's menu lives in an Instagram Story highlight, グランドメニュー, which cannot be fetched). The shop also runs short-run seasonal crepes — e.g. a three-portion ゴリのチョコバナナ and a とろけるバニラのショコラベリーフレンチ, both ¥1,500, in March 2026 — so check the counter for the current limited item. Context worth knowing: 'Ephemere' is French for 'fleeting/short-lived', and the shop means it — it is run by three students from Toba National College of Maritime Technology's advanced course as a fixed-term venture that closes in February 2027. Takeaway only, cash or PayPay, on the 2nd floor of Toba Ichibangai right in front of Toba Station; eating while walking is banned inside the building, so there is a seating space beside the shop. Open Mon and Fri-Sun 13:00 to the mall's closing time, closed Tue-Thu.

items.en: The plain one — a hot crepe with butter and dusted sugar, nothing else
items.section: クレープ / Crepes
items.note: The classic 'sucre' crepe and the best way to judge the batter. Cheapest item on the board.

items.en: Savoury crepe with ham, melted cheese and cracked black pepper
items.section: クレープ / Crepes
items.note: The only savoury item — a nod to the Breton galette that crepes come from, which is traditionally the savoury half of the pair.

items.en: Crepe wrapped around grilled mochi rice cake, nori seaweed and a piece of rice cracker — sweet-savoury and very chewy
items.section: クレープ / Crepes
items.note: The most local thing on the menu: the nori is harvested off Toshi-jima, the fishing island out in Toba Bay. Isobe-maki (mochi wrapped in nori) is a standard Japanese snack; this puts it in a crepe.

items.en: Chocolate sauce, banana and whipped cream
items.section: クレープ / Crepes
items.note: Listed by the shop as the number-one seller with children — the default Japanese crepe-stand order.

items.en: Crepe filled with apple and topped with shards of crisp pastry, so it eats like an apple pie
items.section: クレープ / Crepes
items.note: The pastry topping is added at the counter so it stays crunchy.

items.en: Ise green tea kneaded into the crepe batter, filled with sweet azuki bean paste, shiratama rice dumplings and matcha chocolate
items.section: クレープ / Crepes
items.note: The shop's signature and the priciest item. 'Kintoki' on a Japanese dessert menu means sweetened azuki beans. Mie is a major tea prefecture, so the Ise-cha in the batter is a local ingredient, and it makes the crepe noticeably chewier and less sweet than the others.
